reason: E1 directly shows a fracture mode change from ductile transgranular at 25°C to mixed intergranular at 700°C in a single-phase HEA, supporting the transition premise. E2 demonstrates that a dual-phase variant with pre-existing Cr-rich precipitates avoids intergranular embrittlement and retains ductility at 600–700°C, supporting the sequestration and retained ductility premises. However, neither passage provides direct evidence of nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, Mn to grain boundaries or its effect on cohesion; the mechanism is inferred rather than directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Stress/temperature induces nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, Mn to grain boundaries in single-phase HEA
This segregation reduces grain boundary cohesion and promotes intergranular cracking
Pre-existing Cr-rich precipitates can sequester embrittling elements and inhibit their segregation
The untreated alloy transitions from ductile transgranular to brittle intergranular fracture at intermediate temperatures
The GB-engineered variant retains higher toughness and ductility under the same conditions
